children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a positive start on October 29, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is up about 55 points at 22,789 in early trade.

Indian benchmark indices ended lower on October 28, with the Nifty closing around the 22,700 mark, dragged down by selling in information technology and oil and gas stocks.
Caution ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision and Brent crude prices holding around $115 per barrel following an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery further weighed on investor sentiment.
At close, the Sensex was down 352.64 points or 0.48 percent at 73,246.03, and the Nifty was down 50.90 points or 0.22 percent at 22,698.85.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Up)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 22,789 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Mixed)
Asian indices were trading mixed in the early Thursday trade, with Kospi down 2 percent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 Stock Average gained as strong domestic AI earnings helped offset mixed tech earnings in US markets. Investors will be watching for Samsung Electronics earnings later in the morning.
US Equities (Rise)

US stock indexes advanced on Wednesday after the US Federal ​Reserve left its key policy rate unchanged, as widely expected, leaving investors betting on a rate hike at its next monetary ‌policy meeting in December.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 97.53 points, or 0.19%, to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 gained 21.37 points, or 0.28%, to 7,743.97 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 72.04 points, or 0.27%, ​to 26,549.85.
Dollar Index (Up)

The US dollar steadied on Thursday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates as expected while hinting upcoming inflation data would influence future policy moves, leaving investors uncertain about the rates outlook.
US Bond Yield (Flat)
The Treasury yield curve steepened after Warsh started his press conference.
Yields on 10-year Treasuries were unchanged at 5.01 percent, while yields on 2-year Treasuries were up marginally at 4.70 percent.
Asian Currencies (Gain)

Asian currencies traded mostly higher against the US dollar, with the South Korean won leading gains by rising 0.744 percent, followed by the Philippine peso, which advanced 0.258 percent. The Malaysian ringgit, Thai baht, Singapore dollar, Taiwan dollar and Chinese renminbi also posted modest gains.
Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah weakened 0.154 percent, while the Japanese yen slipped 0.038 percent against the dollar.
Crude (Slips)
Oil dropped as traders assessed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran.
Brent fell toward $114 a barrel after rising by more than 1% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was
near $102 a barrel.
Gold (Down)
Gold dipped after the Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged and offered little guidance on its next move, leaving traders guessing over the prospect of a hike before year-end.
Bullion fell as much as 0.4% to near $4,050 an ounce, after three days of modest gains.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 in favor of holding its benchmark federal funds rate, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank would likely reduce the number of interest-rate decisions to six from eight per year — a move that analysts said could foster more uncertainty.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak on October 28, purchasing equities worth Rs 871 crore, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) also turned net buyers, investing Rs 643 crore in equities during the session.
